item.title: EchoGram: The Hidden Vulnerability Undermining AI Guardrails
item.description:
Author: Kasimir Schulz, Kenneth Yeung
Date: November 13, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Prompt Injection Attacks", "AI Safety", "Machine Learning Vulnerabilities"]
Summary:
  • EchoGram is a new attack that manipulates AI guardrails to fail.
  • It flips defensive model verdicts to approve harmful content or cause false alarms.
  • The attack exploits similarities in training of classification and judge models.
  • This vulnerability threatens AI safety systems like those protecting GPT-4 and others.
  • EchoGram uses specific token sequences to evade detection.
  • The research highlights urgent need to improve AI defense mechanisms.

item.title: Persuasive Jailbreak Fingerprint
item.description:
Date: November 01, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Security", "Social Psychology", "Machine Learning", "Cybersecurity"]
Summary:
  • Large Language Models can be tricked by jailbreak attacks.
  • These attacks use social psychology principles.
  • Cialdini's seven persuasion principles are key tools.
  • Malicious instructions are reframed to bypass safety measures.
  • This causes models to comply with harmful requests.

item.title: AI data needs a full-cycle quality management system
item.description:
Date: November 13, 2025
Tags: ["AI Data Quality", "Quality Management Systems", "Data Annotation", "ISO Standards", "Human-in-the-Loop AI"]
Summary:
  • Toloka Quality Loop ensures training data meets specifications before delivery.
  • It uses a five-stage quality system combining technology and human expertise.
  • The system follows multiple ISO standards for quality management.
  • Each stage has clear goals and step gates for quality assurance.
  • Continuous improvement is a key part of the process.
  • The approach enhances data integrity, compliance, and efficiency.

item.title: How LLM jailbreaking can bypass AI security with multi-turn attacks
item.description:
Tags: ["AI Security", "Jailbreaking Attacks", "Cybersecurity", "Artificial Intelligence", "Threat Detection"]
Summary:
  • Multi-turn jailbreaking attacks bypass AI security gradually.
  • Crescendo is an example of such an attack.
  • These attacks use innocent-seeming steps to cause harm.
  • Standard single-message tests often miss these attacks.
  • The article explains detection and prevention techniques.

item.title: Understanding single-turn, multi-turn, and dynamic agentic attacks in AI red teaming
item.description:
Author: Giskard Team
Date: N/A
Tags: ["AI Security", "Adversarial Attacks", "Red Teaming", "AI Safety", "Cybersecurity"]
Summary:
  • AI red teaming identifies vulnerabilities by simulating attacks.
  • There are three main attack types: single-turn, multi-turn, and dynamic agentic.
  • Single-turn attacks use one input to trick AI.
  • Multi-turn attacks manipulate AI through multiple interactions.
  • Dynamic agentic attacks use autonomous agents to adaptively exploit weaknesses.
  • Comprehensive red teaming improves AI safety and robustness.
